title: Back-Channel Communication Can Be Toxic
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece examines back-channeling, the practice of venting disagreement privately after a meeting rather than raising it openly, and how it erodes team trust over time. It argues that when leaders model this behavior with trusted colleagues, team members mirror it, creating a culture where real disagreement never surfaces where it could actually shape decisions. The article warns that anyone who hears a leader's private complaints about others will eventually assume they, too, are discussed behind their back. The recommended fix is building a team culture where dissent is actively invited and expressed openly, and where leaders explicitly refrain from back-channeling themselves.
points: Back-channeling is defined as expressing disagreement privately after a meeting instead of in the room where it could influence the decision.
When leaders back-channel with trusted colleagues, team members learn to do the same, spreading distrust through the team.
Reserving disagreement for private, after-the-fact conversations robs the team of its ability to work through conflict in a healthy way.
Anyone who hears a leader's back-channel complaints about others will assume the same is said about them.
The remedy is creating an open, safe culture where disagreement is invited during the meeting itself, not after it.
quotes: Complaining about others when they aren’t present is a team sport in some organizations.
this back-channel method of expressing how we really feel about decisions and people can undermine the trust and goodwill needed for teams to perform effectively
Back-channeling is a form of passive-aggressive behavior that just about everyone engages in at one time or another.
Rather than express disagreement “in the room,” where ideas and advocacy can influence decisions, team members use the back channel to express their true views.
leaders who complain about team members with us will, at some point, talk negatively about us to other team members
Don’t let back-channel communication rent space on your team. Raise the rent and ask everyone to disagree openly.
